Frequently Asked Questions

Common Questions About PPC Management Services and How They Drive Business Growth

1. What is PPC Management?

PPC (Pay-Per-Click) management is the professional management of paid advertising campaigns on Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn, and other platforms. A PPC manager handles campaign strategy, keyword research, audience targeting, ad creation, bid management, landing page optimization, and performance reporting to maximize ROI on your ad spend.

2. How much should I spend on PPC?

PPC budget depends on your industry, competition, and business goals. We work with budgets starting from ₹30,000/month. We recommend starting with a test budget, identifying what works, and scaling from there. Our team will advise on the optimal starting budget and growth trajectory during your free audit call.

3. How quickly does PPC generate results?

PPC can generate leads and sales from day one — it's one of the fastest digital marketing channels. The first 30-60 days are typically an optimization phase where we gather data, test audiences and copy, and refine targeting. Most clients see significant ROAS improvements within 60-90 days of campaign launch.

4. Which PPC platforms do you manage?

We manage PPC campaigns on Google Ads (Search, Display, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube), Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram), LinkedIn Ads, and Microsoft Advertising (Bing Ads). We recommend the right platform mix based on your target audience and business goals.

5. Do you manage landing pages too?

Yes. Landing page quality is critical to PPC success — even great ads fail if the landing page does not convert. We provide landing page audits, optimization recommendations, and can design and build dedicated PPC landing pages as part of our service to maximize your conversion rates.

6. How do you prevent budget waste?

We prevent waste through comprehensive negative keyword management, precise audience targeting, geographic and time-of-day bid adjustments, regular search term analysis, quality score optimization, and daily campaign monitoring to catch and fix issues before they drain your budget.

7. What is ROAS and what should I target?

ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) measures revenue generated per rupee spent on ads. A 5x ROAS means you earn ₹5 for every ₹1 spent. Target ROAS varies by industry — eCommerce businesses typically target 4-8x, while service businesses focus on cost per lead. We establish the right targets for your business during onboarding.

8. Will you have access to our ad accounts?

Yes — we require access to your existing Google Ads or Meta Ads accounts (or create new ones for you). We recommend you maintain account ownership. We operate via manager account access, so we manage campaigns without taking ownership of your data or campaign history.

9. How do you report on PPC performance?

We provide monthly PPC performance reports covering total spend, clicks, impressions, CTR, conversions, cost per conversion, and ROAS with campaign-level breakdowns. We also provide access to a live reporting dashboard so you can monitor performance in real-time between monthly reports.

10. What is your PPC management fee?

We charge a flat monthly management fee based on your ad spend and campaign complexity — not a percentage of spend, so we are incentivized to maximize results, not inflate your budget. Contact us for a custom pricing proposal based on your specific needs and goals.

11. What is Quality Score and why does it matter?

Quality Score is Google's rating (1-10) of the relevance and quality of your keywords, ads, and landing pages. A higher Quality Score means lower cost-per-click and better ad positions — meaning you pay less and appear higher than competitors with lower scores. Our PPC specialists focus on improving Quality Scores through tightly themed ad groups, highly relevant ad copy, and conversion-optimized landing pages that match user search intent.

12. How do you prevent click fraud on PPC campaigns?

Click fraud — where bots or competitors repeatedly click your ads to drain your budget — is a real concern. We use IP exclusion for suspicious sources, monitor traffic quality metrics, use Google's built-in invalid click detection, and implement third-party click fraud protection tools where needed. Regular analysis of click patterns and conversion rates helps us identify and eliminate fraudulent traffic quickly to protect your ad budget.

13. What is the difference between PPC and SEM?

PPC (Pay-Per-Click) is a specific type of online advertising where you pay each time someone clicks your ad. SEM (Search Engine Marketing) is a broader term that encompasses all paid search advertising activities — of which PPC is the most common form. While PPC technically refers to any pay-per-click model across display, social, and search, SEM typically refers specifically to paid search ads on Google and Bing. In practice, the terms are often used interchangeably in the context of Google Ads campaigns.

14. How does Google determine where my PPC ads appear?

Google uses an Ad Auction system to determine which ads show for each search query and in what position. The auction considers your Maximum Bid (the highest you're willing to pay per click), your Quality Score (Google's rating of your ad's relevance, expected CTR, and landing page experience, scored 1-10), and your Ad Rank Extensions (additional ad features like sitelinks and callouts). The highest Ad Rank wins the top position — meaning a lower bid with a high Quality Score can outrank a higher bid with a low Quality Score. This is why optimization is so critical.

15. What is a good click-through rate (CTR) for PPC ads?

Average Google Ads CTR varies significantly by industry and ad position. Search ads typically see 3-5% CTR on average, though high-intent industries like legal, healthcare, and financial services can see 6-10%. Display ads average 0.1-0.3%. A CTR significantly above your industry benchmark usually indicates highly relevant, compelling ad copy. However, CTR should always be evaluated alongside conversion rate — a high CTR with a low conversion rate indicates a disconnect between ad promise and landing page delivery.

16. Should I run Google Ads or Meta Ads for my business?

The right choice depends on where your customers are in their buying journey. Google Ads captures demand — people actively searching for your product or service right now. Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram) creates demand — it reaches people based on interests and demographics, showing them products they might not have searched for yet. B2C businesses selling visual products (fashion, home, food) often perform better on Meta. B2B businesses and service providers typically see stronger ROI on Google. Most businesses benefit from running both simultaneously, using each platform's strengths at different stages of the funnel.

17. What is remarketing and why does it matter for PPC?

Remarketing (or retargeting) allows you to show ads specifically to people who have already visited your website or interacted with your brand. These audiences are your most valuable PPC targets because they already know who you are — they just need another nudge to convert. Remarketing campaigns consistently deliver higher conversion rates and lower CPAs than cold-audience campaigns. We set up remarketing audiences across Google Display, YouTube, Meta, and LinkedIn — creating strategic follow-up sequences that re-engage high-intent visitors until they convert.

18. How long does it take for PPC campaigns to become profitable?

Most PPC campaigns can generate leads from day one, but achieving strong profitability typically takes 60-90 days. The first 30 days involve setting up, launching, and gathering initial data. Days 30-60 involve testing ad copy, audiences, and bidding strategies based on early data. By days 60-90, we have enough data to identify top performers, reallocate budget to winning campaigns, and achieve consistent ROAS improvement. Competitive industries with high CPCs may take slightly longer to optimize to profitability.

19. Can small businesses compete with large brands on Google Ads?

Yes — and this is one of the great equalizers of PPC. While large brands have bigger budgets, smaller businesses can compete effectively through smarter targeting. Strategies include: focusing on long-tail keywords with lower CPCs that large brands overlook, targeting specific geographic areas where you have competitive advantages, using highly specific audience targeting to reach high-intent prospects, achieving better Quality Scores through more relevant landing pages, and dominating local search terms where brand name matters less than proximity and relevance. Smart, focused PPC often outperforms big-budget campaigns with poor targeting.

20. What happens if I need to pause or reduce my PPC budget?

One of PPC's greatest advantages is complete budget control. You can pause campaigns at any time, and your ads will immediately stop showing — unlike SEO, there is no delay. Reducing budget simply means your ads show less frequently or stop after a daily limit is reached. However, be aware that pausing campaigns causes you to lose the optimization data and algorithmic learning Google and Meta have built for your campaigns — resuming after an extended pause means a period of re-optimization. If budget is a concern, we recommend reducing rather than fully pausing to maintain campaign momentum.
